beats.say: A razor sells for $5, yet you never stop paying.
Buy the razor alone, no blades included.
Buy a razor plus a few starter blades.
Buy a razor plus a massive bundle of blades.
Buy just a single blade replacement.
Year one: 51 razors, 168 blades sold. Looks lopsided.
But the razor is a loss leader; the real profit lives in blades.
In year two, sales jumped to 90,884 razors, all needing blades.
Each blade costs extra, so the $5 handle becomes a gateway to endless purchases.
The razor hooks you, then the blade subscription fuels the revenue.
You see it everywhere - a coffee shop sells a $2 mug, then $0.30 coffee pods.
A gym offers a $30 starter kit, then $5 per class pass.
Because the starter kit is cheap, the add-on feels like the smart choice.
Watch the first purchase; the recurring add-on is where the money hides. Follow for more.
